sentences.sentence: Pronunciation: sye kloe BEN za preen Brand names: Flexeril , Tonmya , Amrix , Fexmid Dosage form: immediate-release tablet (5 mg, 7.5 mg, 10 mg), extended-release capsule (15 mg, 30 mg), sublingual tablet (2.8 mg) Drug class: Skeletal muscle relaxants
Medically reviewed by Melisa Puckey, BPharm .
Last updated on Aug 14, 2026.
Cyclobenzaprine is a prescription muscle relaxant used short-term to relieve muscle spasms caused by sprains, strains, and injuries, including low back and neck pain.
It is used together with rest and physical therapy to help relieve the pain, tenderness, and limited movement caused by muscle spasm.
Cyclobenzaprine is also used to treat fibromyalgia in adults, where it can help reduce pain.
For fibromyalgia, it is taken as a sublingual (under the tongue) tablet at bedtime under the brand name Tonmya.
In clinical trials, Tonmya significantly reduced fibromyalgia pain compared with placebo over 14 weeks, and close to half of treated patients achieved at least a 30% improvement in pain.
The Flexeril brand has been discontinued, but cyclobenzaprine is available as generic tablets and as the brand-name products Amrix (extended-release capsules) and Fexmid.
Cyclobenzaprine works by reducing the nerve signals in the brain that drive muscle tone and spasm, which allows tight, overactive muscles to relax.
It acts within the central nervous system, primarily at the level of the brain stem, and does not act on the muscles themselves or at the junction between nerves and muscle.
1,2 Because cyclobenzaprine works through the nervous system in this way, it will not relieve muscle spasm caused by central nervous system disease, such as cerebral palsy or spinal cord disease.
The way cyclobenzaprine works in fibromyalgia is not known.
Laboratory studies show it blocks several receptor types, including serotonin (5-HT2A), histamine, and muscarinic receptors.

Cyclobenzaprine is chemically related to tricyclic antidepressants such as amitriptyline, which explains several of its side effects (such as drowsiness and dry mouth) and some of its most important drug interactions.

MAO inhibitors.
Do not take MAO inhibitors, including isocarboxazid, linezolid, phenelzine, rasagiline, selegiline, and tranylcypromine with cyclobenzaprine.
Dangerously high fever, seizures, and deaths have occurred when cyclobenzaprine or similar drugs were combined with these medicines.
Serotonin syndrome.

Cyclobenzaprine can cause a serious condition called serotonin syndrome when taken with certain other medicines, especially antidepressants (SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclics), tramadol, bupropion, meperidine, and verapamil.
Get medical help right away if you have agitation, hallucinations, fever, sweating, shivering, fast heart rate, muscle stiffness or twitching, loss of coordination, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea.
Drowsiness and alcohol.
Cyclobenzaprine can impair your thinking and reactions, and this effect is stronger with alcohol or other medicines that cause drowsiness.
Do not drive or do anything that needs alertness until you know how it affects you.
Pregnancy: If you use Tonmya for fibromyalgia.
Based on animal studies, Tonmya may increase the risk of neural tube defects (a type of birth defect affecting the spine) if used in early pregnancy.
Do not use Tonmya in the two weeks before conception or during the first trimester.
See the Pregnancy section below.
You should not take cyclobenzaprine if you are allergic to it, or if you have:
hyperthyroidism (overactive thyroid);
heart block, a heart rhythm disorder, or congestive heart failure; or
had a recent heart attack.
To make sure cyclobenzaprine is safe for you, tell your doctor if you have ever had:
liver disease; 1,2,3
glaucoma or increased pressure in the eye; 1,2,3
a seizure disorder (Tonmya); 3
an enlarged prostate or problems with urination.
The safety and effectiveness of cyclobenzaprine tablets have not been established in children under 15 years of age.
The safety and effectiveness of Tonmya and Amrix have not been established in children of any age.
Cyclobenzaprine builds up to higher levels in older adults and is more likely to cause side effects such as confusion, hallucinations, heart problems, and falls.
In people 65 and older:
Immediate-release tablets should be used only if clearly needed, starting at 5 mg and increasing slowly under medical supervision.

Amrix extended-release capsules are not recommended at all, because blood levels run about 40% higher and the drug stays in the body much longer (half-life of 50 hours versus 32 hours in younger adults).
Tonmya is limited to the lower 2.8 mg dose once daily at bedtime.
Pregnancy guidance differs by product, so check which cyclobenzaprine product you use.
Tonmya (fibromyalgia): Based on animal data, Tonmya may increase the risk of neural tube defects when used two weeks before conception and through the first trimester.
Because neural tube development happens early, often before pregnancy is recognized, avoid Tonmya during this window.
Your healthcare provider should do a pregnancy test before you start Tonmya, and you should use effective contraception during treatment and for two weeks after the final dose.

Immediate-release tablets and Amrix (muscle spasm): available data have not identified a risk of major birth defects or miscarriage, and animal studies at usual doses did not show harm to the fetus, although data are limited.
These products should be used during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant.
Small published reports suggest cyclobenzaprine passes into breast milk in low amounts, but there is no information on effects on a breastfed baby or on milk supply.
Talk with your healthcare provider about the benefits of breastfeeding alongside your need for this medicine.
Cyclobenzaprine is usually taken for up to 2 or 3 weeks for muscle spasm.
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Your doctor may occasionally change your dose.

Extended-release capsules are taken once daily, at about the same time each day.

sentences.sentence: Seek emergency medical attention or call the Poison Help line at 1-800-222-1222.
An overdose of cyclobenzaprine can be fatal, and deliberate overdoses often involve other drugs or alcohol, which raises the danger.
Overdose symptoms may include severe drowsiness, fast heartbeats, tremors, agitation, slurred speech, confusion, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, or hallucinations.
Rare but critical effects include seizures, dangerously low blood pressure, heart rhythm disturbances, and cardiac arrest.
Avoid driving or hazardous activity until you know how cyclobenzaprine will affect you.
It can impair your thinking and reactions, and this effect is stronger with alcohol or other medicines that cause drowsiness.
Avoid drinking alcohol while taking cyclobenzaprine.
The most common cyclobenzaprine side effects are drowsiness, dry mouth, dizziness, fatigue, and headache .
Most side effects are mild and settle as your body adjusts, but cyclobenzaprine can occasionally cause serious heart rhythm effects and serotonin syndrome.
Common cyclobenzaprine side effects may include: 1
drowsiness and tiredness;
dry mouth;
dizziness;
fatigue;
headache;
nausea, indigestion, or constipation;
blurred vision;
unpleasant taste;
nervousness or confusion.
In placebo-controlled trials of the immediate-release tablets, side effects were dose-related, occurring more often with 10 mg than with 5 mg: 1
With Amrix, the most common side effects are dry mouth (up to 14% at 30 mg), dizziness, fatigue, constipation, nausea, indigestion, and drowsiness.

With Tonmya, because it dissolves under the tongue, the most common side effects involve the mouth: reduced feeling or numbness in the mouth (23%), mouth discomfort, abnormal taste, tingling, mouth pain, and canker sores, along with sleepiness, fatigue, and dry mouth.
Mouth-related effects usually begin within minutes of a dose and most resolve within an hour.
Moistening your mouth with sips of water before dosing reduces the risk of numbness.
Tell your healthcare provider if mouth effects are severe.
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to cyclobenzaprine: hives; difficult breathing; swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat; or itching.
Stop taking cyclobenzaprine and call your doctor at once if you have: 1,2,3
fast, pounding, or irregular heartbeats;
chest pain or pressure, or pain spreading to your jaw or shoulder;
sudden numbness or weakness, slurred speech, or balance problems; or
symptoms of serotonin syndrome: agitation, hallucinations, fever, sweating, shivering, fast heart rate, muscle stiffness or twitching, loss of coordination, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea.
Serious side effects, including confusion, hallucinations, and heart problems leading to falls, are more likely in older adults.
Yes, drowsiness is the most common side effect of the tablets, affecting up to 38% of people taking the 10 mg dose in clinical trials.
This is one reason 5 mg is the usual starting dose, since it causes less drowsiness with comparable effectiveness.
Analysis of trial data shows cyclobenzaprine relieves muscle spasm whether or not sedation occurs, so drowsiness is not required for it to work.
Constipation is a known side effect, reported in 1% to 3% of people taking the immediate-release tablets and up to 3% of people taking Amrix 30 mg in clinical trials.
It results from the drug's anticholinergic (drying) effects, the same mechanism behind dry mouth and blurred vision.
This is not a complete list of side effects, and others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may report side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

The most serious cyclobenzaprine (Flexeril) drug interactions are with MAO inhibitors, which must never be combined with cyclobenzaprine, and with antidepressants and other serotonergic medicines, which can cause serotonin syndrome.
Cyclobenzaprine also interacts with alcohol and other medicines that cause drowsiness, making sedation worse.
Other medicines and substances that interact with cyclobenzaprine include: 1,2,3
MAO inhibitors such as isocarboxazid, linezolid, phenelzine, rasagiline, selegiline, and tranylcypromine (contraindicated; do not use within 14 days);
antidepressants of any kind, including SSRIs, SNRIs, and tricyclics (risk of serotonin syndrome);
bupropion, tramadol, or meperidine;
verapamil;
alcohol;
opioid medicines, sleeping pills, other muscle relaxers, and medicines for anxiety or seizures;
barbiturates and other CNS depressants;
anticholinergic medicines;
guanethidine or similar blood pressure medicines;
cold or allergy medicines containing an antihistamine.
Cyclobenzaprine may increase the risk of seizures in people taking tramadol, and may block the blood pressure-lowering effect of guanethidine and similar drugs.
Tell your doctor about all your other medicines.
This list is not complete, and other drugs may interact with cyclobenzaprine, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.

sentences.sentence: Flexeril was the original brand name for cyclobenzaprine and remains the name many people know it by.

The Flexeril brand has been discontinued and is no longer on the marke t, but this was a commercial decision, not a safety withdrawal: generic cyclobenzaprine tablets containing the same active ingredient remain widely available and inexpensive.
Current brand names include Amrix (15 mg and 30 mg extended-release capsules taken once daily), Fexmid (7.5 mg tablets), and Tonmya (2.8 mg sublingual tablets for fibromyalgia, approved August 2025).
Is cyclobenzaprine a muscle relaxer?
Yes.
Cyclobenzaprine belongs to the class of medicines called skeletal muscle relaxants.
It relieves muscle spasm from acute painful muscle and skeletal conditions by acting in the central nervous system, not on the muscles directly.
What is cyclobenzaprine 10 mg used for?
The 10 mg tablet is used short-term (2 to 3 weeks) to relieve muscle spasm from acute painful conditions such as sprains and strains, alongside rest and physical therapy.
Treatment usually starts at 5 mg three times a day, increasing to 10 mg three times a day only if needed.
Is 10 mg of cyclobenzaprine strong?
10 mg is the highest recommended single dose of the tablet.
Clinical trials showed the 5 mg dose relieves muscle spasm about as well as 10 mg with less drowsiness, which is why 5 mg three times a day is the usual starting dose.
Does Tonmya work right away for fibromyalgia?

Tonmya starts at a lower dose for the first two weeks before increasing to the full dose, and in clinical trials pain relief was measured over 14 weeks of treatment, with benefits over placebo emerging progressively during that period.
